extracted.intended_audience: State environmental agencies (and Tribes) preparing CAA section 111(d) state plans; EGU owners/operators and EPA reviewers
extracted.subtask_short: state plans for EGU emission guidelines
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for states (and Tribes) to develop and submit state plans implementing the EPA's emission guidelines for existing fossil fuel-fired electric generating units (EGUs) under CAA section 111(d), including methodologies for presumptive standards, compliance mechanisms, and required plan components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain stringency of EPA's BSER determination
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must achieve an equivalent level of emission reduction to the degree of emission limitation achievable through application of the BSER as determined by the EPA; standards of performance that states establish must be no less stringent than the presumptive standards of performance in the applicable emission guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To find a state plan 'satisfactory,' the plan must address each affected EGU and achieve at least the level of emission reduction that would result if each affected EGU were achieving its presumptive standard of performance, after accounting for any application of RULOF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not count non-affected-source reductions toward affected EGU compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Emissions reductions from sources not affected by the final emission guidelines may not be counted towards compliance with either a source-specific or aggregate standard of performance for affected EGUs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plans may not account for emission reductions at non-affected fossil fuel-fired EGUs or emission reductions due to the operation or installation of other electricity-generating resources not subject to these emission guidelines for the purposes of demonstrating compliance with affected EGUs' standards of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify each affected EGU and assign into subcategory
rubrics_metrics.description: A state must identify each affected EGU in the state and specify into which subcategory each affected EGU falls when establishing standards of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once assigned, the state uses the corresponding methodology for that subcategory to establish the presumptively approvable standard of performance for each affected EGU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source-specific standard of performance and compliance schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: For each affected EGU within the state plan, the state plan must include a standard of performance and a compliance schedule specific to that individual unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coal-fired affected EGUs must have increments of progress in the state plan and, if relying on permanent cessation, an enforceable commitment and reporting obligations and milestones. State plans must also specify test methods and procedures for determining compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptive baseline: continuous 8-quarter period from part 75 within prior 5 years
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish baseline emission performance for an affected EGU (except low-load natural gas/oil subcategories), a state will use the CO2 mass emissions and corresponding electricity generation data from any continuous 8-quarter period from 40 CFR part 75 reporting within the 5-year period immediately prior to the date the final rule is published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the 8 quarters, divide total CO2 emissions (pounds) by total gross electricity generation (MWh) to calculate baseline CO2 emission performance in lb CO2/MWh. States should choose the most representative continuous 8-quarter period; the EPA will defer to a state's reasonable exercise of discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline for low-load natural gas/oil: use heat input over 8 quarters
rubrics_metrics.description: For affected EGUs in the low-load natural gas-fired or low-load oil-fired subcategory, states will use CO2 mass emissions and corresponding heat input from any continuous 8-quarter period from 40 CFR part 75 reporting within the 5-year period immediately prior to publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the 8 quarters, divide total CO2 emissions (pounds) by total heat input (MMBtu) to calculate baseline CO2 emission performance in lb CO2/MMBtu.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale and guidance on choosing baseline period
rubrics_metrics.description: States may choose the most representative continuous 8-quarter period within the 5-year lookback to avoid skew from atypical operating periods; using total mass and total generation/heat input averages out short-term variability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach reduces need for data sorting/filtering and provides certainty and transparency. Instances needing alternate baseline methodology are expected to be limited to anticipated changes in operation; if varying baseline results in a less stringent standard, the state must use RULOF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of degree of emission limitation to baseline
rubrics_metrics.description: For each subcategory, calculate the presumptively approvable standard by applying the subcategory's degree of emission limitation (as determined by the BSER) to the source-specific baseline emission performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example methodology provided for long-term and medium-term coal subcategories (see respective entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual compliance demonstration and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance must be demonstrated annually; the compliance period corresponds to one calendar year and the compliance demonstration must occur by March 1 of the following year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: For a unit with compliance date January 1, 2030, the first compliance period is January 1–December 31, 2030, with demonstration by March 1, 2031.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards may be rate-based or mass-based; translation required for mass-based
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards of performance must be established as either a rate or, for certain subcategories, a mass of emissions. If a state chooses mass-based compliance, it must first calculate the rate-based emission limitation that corresponds to the presumptive standard and then explain how it translated that rate-based limitation into the mass constituting the EGU's standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must document the conversion methodology when incorporating compliance flexibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptively approvable standards when following EPA methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Where states use the EPA-prescribed methodology for establishing standards of performance for a subcategory, those established standards will be presumptively approvable when included in a state plan submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the EPA methodology yields standards that achieve the requisite degree of emission limitation and meet statutory/regulatory requirements in section 111(a)(1) and 40 CFR 60.24a(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: States may deviate to more stringent standards without RULOF
rubrics_metrics.description: States may deviate from the EPA methodology to apply a more stringent standard of performance to a particular affected EGU without applying RULOF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a state may require a medium-term coal unit to co-fire 50% natural gas (instead of 40%) without invoking RULOF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of RULOF to apply less stringent standards or longer schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: States may apply less stringent standards of performance or longer compliance schedules to particular affected EGUs in certain circumstances by considering and applying the RULOF mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RULOF is designed to address anticipated changes in operation that would make historical baseline non-representative, and to allow less stringent outcomes when justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term coal-fired subcategory BSER and calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: For long-term coal-fired steam generating units the BSER is CCS with 90 percent capture, expressed as 90 percent capture of the mass of CO2 in the flue gas and an 88.4 percent reduction in emission rate (lb CO2/MWh-gross) on an annual basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To calculate the presumptively approvable standard: multiply the baseline lb CO2/MWh by the complement (0.116). Example: baseline 2,000 lb CO2/MWh → standard 232 lb CO2/MWh (2,000 × 0.116). Affected long-term coal EGUs must comply with federally enforceable increments of progress (see section X.C.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Medium-term coal-fired subcategory BSER and calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: For medium-term coal-fired units that commit to permanently cease operations before January 1, 2039, the BSER is 40 percent natural gas co-firing on a heat input basis, which translates to a 16 percent reduction in emission rate (lb CO2/MWh) compared to baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To calculate the presumptively approvable standard: multiply the baseline by the complement (0.84). States must include enforceable commitments to cease operating before January 1, 2039; the commitment must specify the calendar date and be enforceable by the state (e.g., state rule, agreed order, permit). Upon EPA approval the commitment becomes federally- and citizen-enforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to remove coal-firing capability for certain gas/oil units
rubrics_metrics.description: For steam generating units that are natural gas- or oil-fired but retain the capability to fire coal, or that fired coal during the 5-year period prior to publication, or will fire coal after publication and before January 1, 2030, the state plan must include a requirement to remove the capability to fire coal before January 1, 2030.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies because subcategory applicability is determined retrospectively and ensures consistent application of subcategory standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcategorization by load for natural gas- and oil-fired units
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural gas- and oil-fired steam generating units are subcategorized by load level (base load, intermediate load, and low load), and standards for these subcategories are based on BSERs that do not require add-on controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because applicability is retrospective, states do not need enforceable utilization commitments to limit EGUs to a single subcategory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance metric for low-load gas/oil subcategories: lb CO2/MMBtu
rubrics_metrics.description: For affected EGUs in the low-load natural gas- and oil-fired subcategory, compliance is demonstrated based on lb CO2/MMBtu by dividing total reported CO2 mass emissions by total reported heat input during the calendar-year compliance period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For all other subcategories compliance is based on lb CO2/MWh (total CO2 mass divided by total electric generation for the calendar-year compliance period).

rubrics_metrics.name: Increments of progress, milestones, and reporting for controls and closures
rubrics_metrics.description: States must establish increments of progress for affected EGUs installing control technology, and must set milestones and reporting obligations for affected EGUs that plan to permanently cease operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coal-fired affected EGUs in particular must have increments of progress in the state plan; enforceable commitments to cease operation must include reporting obligations and milestones enforceable by the state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing, monitoring, and reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must specify test methods and procedures for determining compliance with standards of performance and include applicable testing, monitoring, and reporting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For modified steam generating units subject to standards, the EPA proposed and is finalizing the same testing, monitoring, and reporting requirements as currently in 40 CFR part 60, subpart TTTT (and updated referenced test methods where finalized).

rubrics_metrics.name: Large modification standard for coal-fired steam generating units
rubrics_metrics.description: For steam generating units that undertake a 'large modification' (physical change or method of operation resulting in >10% increase in hourly CO2 emissions compared to the highest hourly emissions in the prior 5 years), the BSER is amended to mirror the BSER for long-term coal-fired units (CCS with 90% capture), with a degree of emission limitation of an 88.4% reduction in emission rate (lb CO2/MWh).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standard of performance for units undertaking large modifications after May 23, 2023, is a unit-specific emission limit determined by an 88.4% reduction in the unit's best historical annual CO2 emission rate (2002 to date of modification). Compliance required upon startup of the modified affected facility or effective date of the final rule, whichever is later; same testing, monitoring, and reporting requirements as subpart TTTT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping for stationary combustion turbines on heat-input standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of stationary combustion turbines subject to the heat input-based standard must maintain records of electric sales to demonstrate they did not sell electricity above the threshold that would trigger the output-based standard of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA is finalizing a specific requirement that owners/operators maintain these records to demonstrate they did not sell electricity above the threshold.
